newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Telefonica signs CRT stock purchase deal.
newsitem.headline: Telefonica signs CRT stock purchase deal.

text.p: Spain's Telefonica de Espana said it signed Thursday an agreement formalizing the purchase of 35 percent of the capital stock of Brazilian state Rio Grande do Sul's telecom CRT.

"The accord marks the Telefonica Group's entry into the Brazilian telecommunications market and consolidates its leadership in the South American free trade zone Mercosur," the company said in a stament.

A group including Telefonica, its Argentine and Chilean units, Citicorp and Brazilian media group RBS won a December 17 tender for the operating stake in CRT with a bid of 681 million reais ($655 million).

Some 55 percent over the base price, the auction results cheered local financial markets, which closely followed the auction as the first opening of Brazil's promising telecom sector to private capital.
The purchase agreement was signed Thursday morning by Telefonica's president, Juan Villalonga, and Rio Grande do Sul Gov. Antonio Britto during a ceremony at the state capital of Porto Alegre.

"Our entry into the Brazilian market represents an important strategic bridge in Latin America, where Telefonica is already working successfully in Argentina, Chile, Peru and other countries," Villalonga was quoted as saying in the statement.

On Wednesday, Villalonga met with in Brasilia with President Fernando Henrique Cardoso and Telefonica officials announced they would invest together with CRT some $1 billion in 1997 to modernize the company.
Telefonica is the world's ninth largest telecom with 10.2 million lines, 910,000 cellular telephone subscribers and 1.1 million cable television clients.
CRT, formally named Companhia Riograndense de Telecomunicacoes, operates 800,000 fixed lines and 170,000 cellular phones and has 1.1 million cable TV clients.

Brazil plans next year to start privatizing its massive telecommunications sector, first by offering cellular telephone concessions then moving to break up and sell off Telebras, Latin America's largest telecom.
